ig_carousel_topic.topic: CLV (closing line value) and why sharps obsess over it
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Why do sharp bettors care more about the closing line than whether they won?
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors judge every bet by the result. Win equals good bet, loss equals bad bet. That's backwards. A coin flip bet at +200 is a great bet even if you lose it. The result and the quality of the decision are separate things.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Closing line value is the real signal. If you bet a team at +145 and the line closes at +115, you beat the market by 30 cents. That gap means the books and sharp money moved toward your side. Over hundreds of bets, positive CLV is the best predictor of long-term profit.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Concrete example: you bet the Over 8.0 at -105. By first pitch, the book has moved it to -118. You captured 13 cents of value before the market corrected. That's 291 basis points of edge, which is exactly how we flag plays on our model.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: Winning bettors track CLV on every play. It tells you if your process is sound, separate from variance. A 54% win rate with consistent positive CLV is a business. A 60% run with negative CLV is a heater.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: CLV separates process from luck. If you're not tracking it, you're flying blind. This is how sharps actually measure performance.
